'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***[[Siege of El Fasher]]
****The [[United Nations]] [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|Human Rights Office]] reports that the [[Rapid Support Forces]] have killed over 782 civilians and wounded over 1,143 others in [[El Fasher]], [[North Darfur]], [[Sudan]], since May, and urges the RSF to halt their incursions into the city. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/20/more-than-700-killed-in-siege-of-sudans-el-fasher-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
****At least 50 people, mostly from the [[Zaghawa people|Zaghawa ethnic group]], have been killed by the Rapid Support Forces in the past week in El Fasher, North Darfur State, Sudan. [https://sudantribune.com/article294873/ (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)]]
***[[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] injure a [[Syria]]n man protesting against the soldiers' presence in [[Ma'ariya]], [[Daraa Governorate]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/20/israeli-forces-fire-at-syrian-protesters-in-deraa-wounding-one (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Fall of the Assad regime]]
*** The United States drops the $10 million terrorism bounty offered for capture of [[Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham]] leader [[Ahmed al-Sharaa|Abu Mohammad al-Julani]] who ousted Assad. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-united-states-austin-tice-assad-de71dc4920d4677fcfb2d31a2b6e6e54 (AP)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/after-damascus-meeting-us-drops-10-million-terror-bounty-for-new-syrian-leader/ (Times of Israel)]
**[[US intervention in the Syrian civil war]]
***[[U.S.]] forces kill regional [[ISIS]] leader Abu Yusif, also known as Mahmud, in an airstrike in [[Deir ez-Zor Governorate]], [[Syria]]. [https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/Press-Release-View/Article/4014610/centcom-forces-kill-isis-leader-during-precision-strike-in-syria/ (US CENTCOM)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[2024 Kursk offensive]]
***A [[Ukriane|Ukrainian]] [[missile]] strike kills six people and injures 10 others in [[Rylsk, Russia|Rylsk]], [[Kursk Oblast]], [[Russia]], according to acting [[Governor of Kursk Oblast|Kursk Oblast governor]] [[Alexander Khinshtein]]. Russia says that it will raise the issue of the missile strike at the [[United Nations Security Council]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-people-were-killed-wounded-ukrainian-missile-attack-kursk-region-2024-12-20/ (Reuters)]
**[[Kryvyi Rih strikes (2022–present)|Kryvyi Rih strikes]], [[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***At least one person is killed and eight others are injured in Russian missile strikes on [[civilian]] infrastructure in [[Kryvyi Rih]] and [[Kyiv]], Ukraine. [https://kyivindependent.com/kryvyi-rih-residential-building-hit-in-russian-rocket-attack-victims-excavated/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')] [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/russian-missile-attack-kyiv-injures-two-damages-buildings-officials-say-2024-12-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**[[Mali War]]
***At least 20 people are killed in attacks on six villages in [[Mali]]'s [[Mopti Region]] by suspected [[Jihadism|jihadists]] linked to [[al-Qaeda]] and the [[Islamic State]], who also destroy property during the assaults. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/over-20-civilians-killed-central-mali-village-attacks-2024-12-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Israel–Hamas war]], [[Israeli settler violence]]
***[[Israel]]i [[Israeli settlement|settlers]] [[arson|set fire]] to a [[mosque]] in [[Marda, Salfit|Marda]], [[Salfit Governorate]], in the [[occupied West Bank]] and [[vandalism|deface]] the building's facade with [[anti-Arab racism|anti-Arab]] statements, including "[[Death to Arabs]]". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/20/israeli-settlers-set-mosque-on-fire-in-occupied-west-bank (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.barrons.com/amp/news/palestinian-officials-accuse-israeli-settlers-of-mosque-arson-in-west-bank-c5cba85b (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[Terrorism in Germany]]
**[[2024 Magdeburg car attack]]
***Five people are killed and over 200 others are injured in a [[vehicle-ramming attack]] at a [[Christmas]] market in [[Magdeburg]], [[Germany]]. The suspected perpetrator is arrested. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/20/two-dead-as-car-ploughs-into-christmas-market-crowd-in-germany (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.blick.ch/breaking-news/anschlag-in-magdeburg-auto-rast-ueber-weihnachtsmarkt-11-tote-60-verletzte-id20431562.html (Blick)]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**The [[Arakan Army]] claims to have captured the [[Tatmadaw]]'s regional headquarters in [[Rakhine State]], [[Myanmar]]. [https://apnews.com/article/myanmar-rakhine-arakan-army-asean-military-thailand-e1fb9ecc90d26571ec04fbc00e94fd77 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Malaysia Airlines Flight 370]]
**[[Search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370]]
***[[Minister of Transport (Malaysia)|Malaysian Minister of Transport]] [[Anthony Loke]] announces a new search effort for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, which went missing in March 2014, to be conducted by American [[autonomous underwater vehicle|marine robotics]] company [[Ocean Infinity]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/malaysia-to-resume-search-for-missing-mh370-plane/a-71115876 (DW)]
*[[Rohingya genocide]]
**The [[Sri Lanka Navy]] rescues 102 [[Rohingya]] refugees, including 25 children, that were found adrift on a [[fishing trawler]] and takes them to [[Trincomalee]], [[Sri Lanka]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/20/sri-lanka-navy-rescues-over-100-rohingya-adrift-in-the-indian-ocean (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/south-asia/sri-lanka-navy-rohingya-refugees-b2667829.html (''The Independent'')]
*Thirty-eight people are killed, 20 people are rescued, and over 100 others remain missing after a [[ferry]] capsizes while crossing the [[Busira River]] in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-boat-capsizes-busira-river-ac222ab809e107b119a8e86f1d5aa3f2 (AP)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/12/22/dozens-dead-after-ferry-capsizes-in-dr-congo-official (Al Jazeera)]
*Eleven people are killed, 45 others are injured and 37 vehicles are destroyed after an [[Liquefied petroleum gas|LPG]] [[tank truck]] catches fire and explodes after a speeding truck crashed into it in [[Jaipur]], [[Rajasthan]], [[India]]. [https://www.thestatesman.com/india/11-burnt-to-death-45-injured-in-lpg-tanker-truck-explosion-in-jaipur-centre-raj-govt-petroleum-co-announce-relief-1503378114.html (''The Statesman'')] 
*Eight people are killed and 18 others are rescued when a [[Motorboat|speedboat]] carrying migrants capsizes off the coast of [[Rhodes]], [[Greece]]. [https://apnews.com/article/greece-migrations-migration-turkey-smuggling-deaths-fe8a791935f8eab2303aa16038939a5f (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Australia–Solomon Islands relations]]
**[[Australia]] agrees to provide [[Solomon Islands]] with financing, training, and infrastructure support worth [[Australian dollar|AU$]]190 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]118 million) over four years to strengthen its [[Royal Solomon Islands Police Force|police force]] as part of a renewed security partnership between the two countries. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20241220-australia-agrees-deal-to-finance-train-solomons-police (France 24)]
*[[Hungary–Poland relations]]
**[[Poland]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Poland)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] summons [[Hungary]]'s ambassador to protest the [[Hungarian government]]'s decision to grant [[Right of asylum|asylum]] to former Polish deputy [[Ministry of Justice (Poland)|justice minister]] [[Marcin Romanowski]], who is wanted under the [[European Arrest Warrant]] for alleged [[Corruption in Poland|corruption]]. Poland also recalls its ambassador to Hungary [[Sebastian Kęciek]] for consultations. [https://apnews.com/article/poland-hungary-asylum-politician-dispute-6c528154f2ca2a67ef45fad333aa1984 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Zagreb school stabbing]]
**A child is killed and seven other people are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] at a [[primary school]] in [[Zagreb]], [[Croatia]]. The 19-year-old perpetrator is arrested. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj6znexl7ljo (BBC News)]
*The [[Inter-American Court of Human Rights]] rules that [[El Salvador]] violated the [[Human rights in El Salvador|human rights]] of a woman denied [[Abortion in El Salvador|an abortion]] during a [[high-risk pregnancy]] in 2013 and orders the country to implement measures allowing abortions in cases where the woman's life is at risk. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/dec/20/el-salvador-abortion-death-ruling (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Guatemala]]n authorities rescue 160 minors from the [[Lev Tahor]] sect in [[Oratorio, Santa Rosa]], amid allegations of [[Human trafficking in Guatemala|human trafficking]], [[forced marriage]], and [[child abuse]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/guatemalan-authorities-rescue-160-children-jewish-lev-tahor-sect-2024-12-21/ (Reuters)]
*The U.S. [[Consumer Financial Protection Bureau]] files a lawsuit against banks [[JPMorgan Chase]], [[Bank of America]], and [[Wells Fargo]] for failing to protect consumers against alleged widespread [[fraud]] on the built-in [[payment system]] [[Zelle]] equating over $870 million. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2024/12/20/us-consumer-watchdog-sues-big-banks-over-widespread-fraud-on-zelle-app (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.freep.com/story/money/personal-finance/susan-tompor/2024/12/20/zelle-bank-of-america-jp-morgan-case-wells-fargo-fraud/77102020007/ (''Detroit Free Press'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 United States federal budget]]
**[[Government shutdowns in the United States]], [[National debt of the United States]], [[United States debt ceiling]]
***A funding [[Bill (United States Congress)|bill]] ensuring full operation of [[Federal government of the United States|the U.S. federal government service]] with an amendment supported by [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Donald Trump]] that would enforce a two-year suspension of the federal debt ceiling is rejected in the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican-majority]] [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]], with multiple Republicans and nearly all [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] opposing the bill. A [[government shutdown]] is expected to occur if no bill is passed by midnight. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cz6l9e3jq7xo (BBC News)]
***[[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Mike Johnson]] reintroduces a funding bill without Trump's debt ceiling suspension, stating that "we will not have a government shutdown". The bill, which will fund the government until March 2025, passes the House by a vote of 336–34 and will now go to the [[United States Senate|Senate]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/12/20/government-shutdown-bill-house-trump-musk/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2025 Belarusian presidential election]]
**[[Estonia]] says that it will not recognize the results of the upcoming presidential election in [[Belarus]], which it claims has already been rigged to ensure that [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] will be re-elected. [https://news.err.ee/1609556065/estonia-will-not-recognize-belarusian-presidential-elections-charade (ERR)]
*In [[Italy]], the [[Meloni government]] survives a [[confidence vote]] in the [[Chamber of Deputies (Italy)|Chamber of Deputies]] on the 2025 budget. [https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/italy-govt-calls-confidence-vote-over-deficit-cutting-2025-budget-2024-12-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sam Hou Fai]] is sworn in as [[Chief Executive of Macau|Chief Executive]] of [[Macau]], succeeding [[Ho Iat Seng]]. [https://gbcode.rthk.hk/TuniS/news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1784304-20241220.htm (RTHK)]
